macro_view.summary: No web search was available, so this view rests only on the data package. DIA fell 8.0% in the week to 2026-11-20 and 8.9% over a month. The selloff hit AI and tech names hardest (NVDA -23%, CRM -17%, GOOGL -10%), along with cyclicals and banks (CAT -15%, GS -14%). Staples and defensives were roughly flat. Rates look restrictive: CPI is running at 4.1% YoY, the 10-year yield is 5.04% and the 2-year is 4.76%, both above a 4.0% fed funds upper bound. The coming week is short because of Thanksgiving, and liquidity is usually thin. I lean modestly toward a short-term rebound in heavily sold, low-P/E large caps. I expect defensives with rich valuations to lag if the market stabilises. The main risk is that forced selling continues. Two things I cannot verify: what caused the selloff, and the company-specific news behind it.

picks_rationale: After an 8% weekly drop in DIA, I tilt toward a short-term reversal in large, liquid names that were sold hardest and now trade on low trailing P/Es: NVDA (13.5), GOOGL (13.9) and GS (11.4). AMZN adds mega-cap exposure at a modest P/E with less extreme drawdown. Thanksgiving-week seasonality is mildly supportive. The key risk is that selling continues, since none of these has a known catalyst inside the window. Defensives that outperformed (WMT, PG, MCD, KO) are ranked lowest.
